ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners against the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade sanctioned persons list, the Samoa FIU criminal and adverse media database, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Additional enhanced due diligence is triggered for any person identified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), family member, or close associate. All screening must be completed and documented within 30 days prior to the incorporation filing date.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Company Registry e-Services Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: International Company names must be in English or Samoan and rendered in the Latin script. Chinese characters or any non-Latin script cannot appear in the registered legal name. A parallel Chinese trade name may be used for branding only but must be clearly stated as an unregistered translation in all commercial documents. The legal name must end with 'Limited' or its approved abbreviation 'Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or licensed registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 business days of the rejection notice, providing evidence of distinctiveness and non-confusion. A statutory declaration must accompany the appeal, together with up to three alternative names. If the Registrar rejects the appeal, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a low-risk international online-retail entity, a virtual office or correspondence address is acceptable for day-to-day mail handling; however, a licensed registered agent in Samoa must maintain the statutory registered office and accept service of legal process. A purely virtual office without a licensed registered agent does not satisfy the International Companies Act 1987.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; the risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a standard ISIC 4791 e-commerce International Company is estimated below 5% per annum, and such inspections are generally triggered only by financial-crime red flags or high-risk activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Company Registry
Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Company Registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public / competent authority of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff or prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO disclosure and PEP/sanctions screening compliance file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed AML/CFT compliance officer or registered agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International courier delivery of original legalized documents to the Samoa registered agent

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: International Company Incorporation Application (Form IC-1) together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; an International Company may issue shares in any currency and is not required to maintain a paid-up capital or escrow account under the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers to the Memorandum and Association hereby agree to subscribe for the initial issued shares of the International Company as set forth in the register of members. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be situated at the address of the licensed registered agent in Samoa, and that said office shall be maintained continuously. RESOLVED that the following persons are appointed as directors and officers of the Company, to serve until replaced by a subsequent resolution. RESOLVED that the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and complete all filings under the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage licensed registered agent and reserve company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry via MCIL-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed company name to the licensed registered agent, who checks availability and files a name reservation request with the Registry. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days. The agent must be appointed to serve as the registered agent of the International Company.
required_dossiers: Certificate of identification for each subscriber
Signed engagement letter appointing the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or conflicts with an existing name, file an alternative name reservation within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent and notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the International Companies Act 1987, including share capital, objects, and governance provisions. Each subscriber must execute the document with witnessed signatures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the governing documents, amend the relevant clauses and re-execute where required within 7 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1, the executed Memorandum and Articles, and the registered agent's certificate through the licensed agent. The application is filed electronically or in paper form as accepted by the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Registry query within 14 days of notice; failure to respond may be cured by submitting an extension request or revised application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay registration fees and obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry / Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official government filing fee of USD 250 through the registered agent or the designated government payment portal. Upon confirmation of payment and final approval, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misallocated or the certificate is delayed, present the receipt to the Registry for verification and expedited issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish corporate registers and statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, maintain the statutory registers including register of members, register of directors and officers, and minute book. Appoint a corporate secretary if required by the company's constitution, and prepare the registered office details for ongoing compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent identifies any incomplete register entry, correct the record and file an amended notice with the Registry where necessary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — non-industrial online retail business under ISIC 4791
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing license required for online retail of 3D printers and consumables

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (Samoa)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no industrial facility, manufacturing process, or environmental hazard
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to an online retail operation; if general municipal waste is generated at office premises, comply with the Waste Management Act 2018 and local Apia municipal waste collection requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to a non-physical online retail operation; if a small office is occupied, comply with the Samoa National Building Code for fire safety, emergency exits, and general workplace health and safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Motootua, Apia, Samoa; official administration and e-filing portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws (SRA e-Services). International company incorporation, licensing, and annual fees are separately administered by the Registrar of International Companies within the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Nexus screening: A Samoan International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt from Samoan income and capital taxes on offshore profits; TIN procurement is obligatory only where the IC (i) makes VAGST-taxable supplies in Samoa, (ii) physically clears goods through Samoan Customs (import VAGST), or (iii) otherwise incurs a Samoan tax liability (e.g. licensed local business). Step 2 - Application: Submit the SRA Application for Tax Registration via SRA e-Services or in person at the SRA taxpayer service centre, attaching (a) the MCIL-issued Certificate of Incorporation of the International Company, (b) certified copy of the charter and memorandum of association, (c) certified copy of the registered office and registered agent confirmation, (d) register of directors and shareholders, (e) letter of appointment of the local registered agent, and (f) a short description of the online retail scope (ISIC 4791). Step 3 - Issuance: SRA validates the application and issues a 9-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN), normally within 10 business days; the same TIN serves income tax, VAGST, and customs accounts. Step 4 - VAGST registration: where annual taxable turnover in Samoa reaches WST 150,000, or where the IC elects voluntary registration, file the VAGST registration within 21 days of the obligation arising and obtain a VAGST registration certificate. No minimum capital, local shareholding, director residency, or physical presence is required for an International Company; the registered agent satisfies statutory presence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: The Samoa International Company operates as a tax-exempt offshore entity under the International Companies Act 1987 (s.175 exemption), outside the scope of the Samoan Income Tax Act 2012. It is treated as non-resident and non-domiciled for Samoan tax purposes, attracting zero income tax on offshore business profits, no capital gains tax, no gift or estate duty, no stamp duty, and no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or management fees paid to non-residents. Samoan-source taxation would arise only where the IC obtains a licence to carry on business in Samoa, where VAGST applies to domestic supplies, or where goods physically enter Samoa and import VAGST and customs duty become exigible.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a US-style check-the-box or elective pass-through/entity-classification regime, nor a hybrid-mismatch deduction election. The statutory options that a Samoan IC may elect are: (1) Voluntary VAGST registration under s.13 of the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 1999, permitting a person making taxable supplies below the WST 150,000 threshold to register and recover input credits; (2) Election to convert an International Company into a domestic company under the International Companies Act 1987, which forfeits the IC tax-exempt status and subjects the entity to normal corporate income tax on worldwide income; (3) Application to the Registrar of International Companies for a licence authorising the IC to carry on business in Samoa, triggering tax residence-type exposure on Samoan-source income and full VAGST obligations; and (4) Election of accounting periods and cash or invoice basis for VAGST returns where sanctioned by the SRA. No anti-hybrid or transparent-entity election exists in Samoan domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) levied under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 1999 (as amended), administered by the Samoa Revenue Authority; border collection is supported by the Samoa Customs Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 150,000 annual value of taxable supplies made in Samoa (VAGST Act 1999, s.12); voluntary registration is available below the threshold and registration is mandatory for a non-resident person making supplies in Samoa that exceed the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, compulsory digital stamping, or nationwide electronic invoicing mandate (B2B or B2C) is currently operative in Samoa. Compliance is return-driven: VAGST-registered persons must file monthly VAGST returns and remit tax electronically through the SRA e-Services portal, and must issue tax invoices, credit notes, and adjustment notes satisfying the content and record-keeping requirements of the VAGST Act 1999 and the Tax Administration Act 2012. Physical export and import transactions are processed through the ASYCUDA World electronic single-window of the Samoa Customs Service; the customs export declaration is the principal control document for export zero-rating. The absence of e-invoicing clearance does not relax the documentary burden at audit, and all backup documentation must be retained for the statutory record period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods, including desktop 3D printers, resin filaments, and maker consumables, are zero-rated at 0% VAGST where the supply is a direct export, namely the supplier exports the goods from Samoa within 28 days after the date of supply and retains conclusive proof of physical exportation. Services qualify as zero-rated exported services where the recipient is a non-resident, the services are delivered for the benefit of a person outside Samoa, and the services are consumed wholly outside Samoa. In the typical Samoan IC drop-ship model, where 3D printers and filaments are procured from overseas factories and shipped directly to foreign end-customers without the goods ever entering Samoa, the supply is outside the scope of Samoan VAGST, because no supply occurs in Samoa; in that case no VAGST registration, zero-rating claim, or input credit arises. Where goods are physically imported into Samoa and subsequently re-exported, import VAGST is payable at the border and can be reclaimed as an input credit against the zero-rated export supply, provided the exporter holds the full export documentation bundle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World electronic export entry) endorsed by the Samoa Customs Service
Commercial sales invoice showing full goods description, quantity, price, Incoterms, and overseas customer identity
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical carriage from Samoa to the stated overseas destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice proving receipt of the foreign currency export proceeds
Purchase order or sales contract, packing list, and any SRA-requested zero-rating support schedule
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to ex-post audit by the Samoa Revenue Authority under the Tax Administration Act 2012 and the VAGST Act 1999. Where the export documentation bundle is incomplete, internally inconsistent, or the goods cannot be matched to an endorsed customs export entry, the SRA will re-characterise the supply as a standard-rated taxable supply, assess VAGST at 15%, and recover the tax together with statutory late-payment penalties that accrue monthly, and shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax avoided for intentional evasion. False zero-rating claims, forged customs entries, fictitious bills of lading, and sham export structures constitute criminal offences attracting fines and imprisonment, retrospective reassessments for extended periods where fraud or evasion is established, and clawback of any VAGST refunds already paid, with interest. The SRA additionally applies anti-avoidance powers and may cancel or suspend VAGST registration and, where applicable, recommend suspension of an International Company licence for serious or repeated non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), constituted under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, acting as the exchange control and monetary authority under the Exchange Control Act 1972 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2021.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed float with active CBS market intervention. Current account transactions through authorized dealers are generally permitted without prior CBS approval, except that amounts exceeding the prescribed threshold require an exchange control declaration on CBS Form EC-1. Capital account inflows and outflows, including equity subscription and dividend repatriation, require prior exchange control approval unless covered by a general permission applicable to International Companies. The WST is not an internationally delivered currency; trade and treasury settlements must clear through USD, AUD, EUR, or TWD correspondent accounts. Dividend profit remittance from the tax-exempt 'WS_IC' is not subject to Samoan withholding tax, but the payor bank will require audited financial statements evidencing distributable reserves and a CBS clearance for exemption from exchange control approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1972, and applicable CBS Notices, all export proceeds arising from online retail sales of goods must be received through an authorized dealer within 90 days from the date of shipment or provision of service. E-commerce receivables from Stripe and Shopify Payments must be repatriated into the IC's CBS-authorized external foreign currency account without unauthorized diversion to personal or third-party accounts. There is no mandatory fixed percentage conversion of export receipts into WST; however, the exporter must either offer the receipts for conversion into WST or justify their retention in an external foreign currency account on bona fide trade grounds, with all supporting invoices, logistics waybills, and platform settlement reports retained for a minimum of seven years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Limited (Samoa Branch)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs are not authorized to carry on deposit-taking, money transmission, or treasury servicing in Samoa without a CBS license under the Financial Institutions Act 1996. Moreover, neither Stripe nor Shopify Payments supports Samoa as a direct merchant jurisdiction, so the compliant treasury architecture requires a merchant-of-record, payment facilitator, or intermediary e-commerce holding entity incorporated in a Stripe-/Shopify-supported jurisdiction (e.g., Hong Kong, Singapore, or United Kingdom). All net collections from such facilitators must be settled via SWIFT into the Samoa IC's external account at a CBS-licensed authorized dealer; holding operating liquidity at any unlicensed offshore EMI creates a regulatory breach, FX evasion presumption, and automatic rejection during Samoan bank KYC underwriting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person verification is the prevailing standard. Samoan licensed banks require at least one authorized signatory director, or a fully identified third-party introducer acceptable to the bank, to undergo face-to-face customer due diligence at a CBS-licensed branch or at an approved overseas office of a FATF-equivalent bank applying agent arrangements. Remote-only account opening is not available to non-resident-owned International Companies in Samoa. Where a key director is offshore, the onboarding bank will accept a notarized passport and proof-of-address package from a recognized introducer bank, together with a compliance-certified board resolution designating the introducing institution to perform verification on its behalf.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee or undisclosed ultimate beneficial ownership over the WS_IC International Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified incorporation certificate and register of members from the licensed registered agent; current certificate of good standing issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); passport copies and residential proof of every natural person holding 10% or more; sworn source-of-wealth statement; six months of personal bank statements of the principal beneficial owner; consent-to-act letters from all directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency global e-commerce settlements from multiple payment aggregators creating transaction provenance opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Granular settlement exports from Stripe and Shopify Payments matched to the IC's bank credits by date, currency, buyer jurisdiction, and gross amount; chargeback and refund ledger showing immaterial dispute ratios; platform KYB records and merchant agreements; monthly reconciliation template mapping each payout to a discrete bank entry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company status combined with a low-risk retail classification used as a pass-through shell
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Physical inventory proof for desktop 3D printers and resin filaments, including commercial invoices, air waybills, bills of lading, and warehouse receipts; live storefront URLs with active catalogues and pricing; supplier purchase orders evidencing real goods flow; customer service tickets and warranty records; trademark and domain registration certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire payments to offshore manufacturers of 3D printers and consumables in high-risk or high-volume jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying supplier contracts and purchase orders; HS-coded commodity descriptions (HS 8443.31 for printers; HS 3916/3920 for filaments) on invoices and customs declarations; packing lists and freight forwarding proof; board resolutions approving each supplier disbursement; annual intercompany transaction summary where group entities are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions-list, or PEP flag hits on the IC name or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Continuous sanctions and adverse media screening report (World-Check or Dow Jones) generated at onboarding and refreshed quarterly; written mitigating explanation of same-name matches; multilingual negative-news searches; ownership-chain affidavit from the registered agent; undertaking letter to notify the bank immediately upon any change of control.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital subscriptions must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's own personal or corporate bank account directly into the WS_IC's external foreign currency account at a CBS-licensed authorized dealer. The payment reference field must state 'Capital Subscription – Samoa IC [Entity Name] Equity Injection'. The IC must issue a board resolution authorizing the share issuance, a CPI-certified updated register of members, and a beneficial ownership declaration. Correspondent banks classify the wire under BOP statistical code 111 (direct investment, equity capital). All supporting documents, bank credit advices, and the CBS Form EC-1 or applicable general permission particulars must be archived to prove that the inflow qualifies as permissible inward direct investment rather than unrelated third-party or trade debt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for desktop 3D printers and resin filaments should use SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for recurring production runs and irrevocable at-sight documentary credits (SWIFT MT700 commercial letters of credit) for bulk procurement. Each disbursement requires the underlying commercial invoice, packing list, HS-coded commodity description, and evidence that the receiving entity is the true supplier of the printed hardware or consumable. Payments are debited from the IC's external account without additional exchange control approval where the trade documents are pre-vetted by the bank; all swift messages must include the purpose code 'Trade Payment – Imports of Goods' to maintain an auditable clearing trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Covered deliverable USD/WST forward contract with a tenor of up to 12 months, executed through a CBS-licensed authorized dealer and supported by underlying import or export trade documentation.
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) in USD/WST booked through a CBS-licensed dealer or an offshore affiliate of such dealer, with net settlement in USD and no physical delivery of Samoan Tala.

Simple USD/WST FX swap combining a spot sale and a matched forward purchase, executed by a CBS-licensed bank against identified trade cashflows, provided the instrument is a plain vanilla contract and not a bespoke cross-currency derivative requiring onshore licensing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return and Annual Government Fee Remittance, submitted by the registered agent with a declaration confirming registered office, directors, members, and beneficial ownership register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based due date; the Annual Return and fee must be completed on or before the anniversary of incorporation. If the anniversary falls on a non-business day, the next business day after the anniversary is treated as the due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a penalty of approximately 10% of the unpaid annual fee for each month or part of a month that the fee remains overdue, capped at the annual fee amount. If the default continues after formal Registry notice, the Registrar may administratively strike the International Company off the register, resulting in loss of corporate personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Certificate confirming that the statutory registers, members' records, and beneficial ownership records have been inspected and are current.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (retained in the company's registered files and produced upon Registrar request)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same anniversary date as the Annual Return and Annual Government Fee Remittance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An inaccurate compliance certificate or materially incomplete statutory registers may trigger a Registrar compliance inspection, monetary penalties, and strike-off proceedings after a final notice. Continued non-compliance by the registered agent may also cause the agent to resign.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Samoa International Company is generally exempt from statutory audit. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only where the company holds a Samoan banking, insurance, or securities licence; where shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting rights validly demand an audit; or where the Registrar exercises investigative powers and directs an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory filing of financial statements is required for a Samoa International Company. Where accounts are voluntarily prepared, the company may apply IFRS, US GAAP, or another recognised accounting framework acceptable to the registered agent; Samoa does not impose a distinct mandatory local GAAP for International Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa International Companies do not file a public annual UBO declaration. The registered agent must maintain a current Beneficial Ownership Register and verify its accuracy at least annually as part of the Annual Return compliance review. Every share allotment or transfer that changes beneficial ownership must be entered in the Register of Members and notified to the registered agent promptly; the registered agent is responsible for updating the Beneficial Ownership Register and ensuring consistency with the underlying share records.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600–US$1,500 per annum, depending on the registered agent, services included, and number of company records maintained.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not a mandatory recurring cost for a tax-exempt International Company engaged in online retail; a voluntary independent audit typically costs US$2,000–US$4,500 depending on transaction volume and file complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (International Company full exemption; standard Samoa resident corporate rate is 27%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax exemption; exemption from dividend withholding tax, interest withholding tax, and royalty withholding tax on distributions; no capital gains tax; no exchange control; no payroll taxes on expatriate employees engaged outside Samoa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return of International Company (Form IC-AR), filed electronically through the Samoa Online Registry System (SONRS) administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration number and full legal name
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact name and number as in the certificate of incorporation; non-resident beneficial owners must not use trade names.
Must be a physical address in Apia maintained by the licensed Samoan registered agent; P.O. boxes are insufficient.
Identify all directors and shareholders, including nominee holders; attach a separate beneficial ownership schedule for non-resident principals if required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of no business conducted in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the IC has not carried on commercial trading, held land, or derived income from sources within Samoa; false declarations trigger immediate loss of tax exemption.
The licensed Samoan registered agent must sign and verify the annual return; foreign directors cannot self-certify.
Confirm payment of the annual government fee to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue; non-payment voids the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 200 plus WST 50 per day of continuing default; prolonged default triggers court-ordered strike-off, forfeiture of assets, and loss of limited liability protection for future claims.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Tax Exemption Declaration and Non-Activity Statement (Form TX-EXD) filed via the Samoa Ministry of Revenue E-Tax Portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 March following the end of the IC's financial year (or within 6 months of the financial year-end if a non-standard accounting period is adopted)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and IC registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the IC's Samoa tax identification number if already issued; otherwise use the company registration number and attach a statement that no tax ID has been issued because of exempt status.

Confirm that the IC has no income sourced from Samoa and no permanent establishment in Samoa; if the entity sells 3D printers or consumables to Samoa customers, exemption may be lost and a normal Samoan tax return may be required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements or summary of transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For dormant or non-Samoa-source entities, attach a statement of no Samoan transactions; for e-commerce operations, summarise gross revenue by country to demonstrate no Samoa-source receipts.
Must be signed by the licensed Samoa agent holding a current certificate; overseas directors may not submit the declaration directly.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: False declaration is an offence under the Crimes Act 2016 (s.75); penalty of up to 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine of WST 20,000, plus mandatory reassessment at the 27% corporate rate on all undeclared Samoa-source income with monthly late-payment penalties of 2%.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Companies under the International Companies Act 2011; the standard statutory dividend withholding tax rate for a Samoa resident company is 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa International Companies distributing dividends, interest, or royalties to non-residents are exempt from Samoan withholding tax and therefore no treaty relief is required. If a Samoa resident company pays such amounts and treaty relief is sought, the beneficial owner must submit Form WHT-R to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue together with an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty counterpart, a statement of beneficial ownership, and a signed treaty entitlement declaration. The Ministry processes the application within 30 days and issues a reduced withholding assessment or exemption certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For payments made by Samoa International Companies, the rate is 0%. For ordinary Samoa resident companies, the domestic withholding rates are 10% for interest and 10% for royalties; under the Samoa-China Double Taxation Agreement, these rates may be reduced to 5% for interest and 5% for royalties, subject to Limitation on Benefits and beneficial ownership rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory transfer pricing documentation thresholds are specified in Samoa's Income Tax Act; international companies are outside the income tax net. If an IC is reclassified as a Samoa resident due to actual management and control in Samoa or a permanent establishment, the Ministry of Revenue may require Local File and Master File on-demand for related-party cross-border transactions exceeding WST 750,000 in annual gross payment.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations impose an economic substance test on ICs undertaking 'relevant activities', including distribution and service centre functions. An online retail operation selling desktop 3D printers and resin filaments is considered a distribution and service centre if it performs procurement, storage, logistics, or customer service through a Samoa branch. The entity must demonstrate a physical office in Samoa, qualified employees, core income-generating activity conducted in Samoa, and adequate operating expenditure. Failure to do so results in loss of tax exemption, penalties, and potential strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false declaration that the International Company has no Samoa-source income while actually soliciting sales to Samoa residents or maintaining a Samoan warehouse, logistics hub, or any dependent agent in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all income at 27% corporate rate; late payment penalty of 2% per month; penalty under Income Tax Act 1974 and Crimes Act 2016 of up to WST 100,000 and 7 years imprisonment; strike-off of the IC and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false declarations lose limited liability; they are personally liable for unpaid taxes, civil restitution, travel bans, and disqualification from serving as directors of any Samoa company for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of nominee shareholders and nominee directors without any authority, no Samoan physical presence, and no capacity to demonstrate core income-generating activity; sales of 3D printers and consumables are merely routed through the Samoa IC without real management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the ESR, a deficiency determination requires a corrected return, loss of exemption, an additional 10% penalty on net income, and deregistration of the IC; the assets may escheat to the Government of Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Registrar may obtain a court order making directors jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid fees, penalties, and applicable taxes; travel bans and prohibition on acting as a director for up to 10 years may also be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a beneficial ownership register, failure to conduct customer due diligence on buyers paying via Stripe or Shopify, acceptance of payments from sanctioned jurisdictions, or processing of suspicious 3D printer/consumable transactions without filing a suspicious transaction report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2018, fines for legal persons up to WST 500,000 and imprisonment of individuals up to 14 years; confiscation of all proceeds linked to the offending transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge or wilful blindness to money laundering or sanctions breaches are personally criminally liable; they may face immediate travel bans, cross-border extradition, and civil forfeiture.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: International Company Regime Abuse / Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misrepresenting the Samoa IC as a tax resident solely to obtain benefits under a double taxation agreement (notably Samoa-China DTA) without satisfying beneficial ownership or Limitation on Benefits clauses; the entity does not have genuine management and control in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive denial of treaty benefits, recovery of under-withheld tax at up to 15%, penalty of 100% of the tax underpaid, and deregistration of the IC for failure to hold a valid annual license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors abstaining from oversight are liable for reckless trading under the Companies Act; the Ministry of Revenue may bring a civil claim for restitution, apply for passport surrender, and obtain a restraint order over personal assets.
